text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian naira currency waxes stronger because of influx of funds from overseas holiday makers; now exchanges at 72 to the dollar from 79 in the previous week, dealers say.
- Big debtors of state telecoms company NITEL flee Nigeria for fear of being prosecuted by task force on telecommunications and postal offences, says task force boss Captain Wole Akinyele.
- Nigerian Export Promotion Council identifies 14 types of fresh fruits, vegetables and flowers in the country with export potential, says its assistant director Aliyu Lawal.

- Foreign minister summons U.S. ambassador and protests over American government official warning about possible bomb blasts at Nigerian airports in last two weeks of December. Nigeria says it was not tipped off officially. A bomb went off a day later.
- Political parties urge military ruler General Sani Abacha to call to order people saying he should contest presidential poll in 1998 aimed at restoring democracy.
- Mortgage bankers appraise performance of their sector in outgoing year and say business has been dull.
- Stock exchange bars 10 brokers for failing to pay for shares they purchased.
- Conglomerate UAC and pharmaceutical firm Beecham announce lower profits, reflecting harsh operating business climate.
- University teachers threaten new strike to press for reinstatement of their colleagues sacked or suspended over a five-month stoppage that ended in October.
- Prices of goods in Nigerian markets fall inspite of Christmas with 50 kg bag of rice selling for about 2,000 naira compared with 3,500 naira at the same time last year.
- Reformed airport authority rakes in two billion naira from various charges by end November, an increase of more than 500 percent from last year.
